How LensPin matches camera photos by time

Last updated November 5, 2026

Understand time matching with four location sources, camera clock offset previews, and reviewing suggestions before saving to Photos.

Four sources on one timeline

LensPin compares camera capture times with four location sources: geotagged iPhone photos from the same trip; geotagged photos from other GPS-equipped cameras; GPX tracks; Apple Health workout routes. Camera photos and optional videos must already be in your Photos library. Nearby reference times and consistent places help support a match; missing clues cannot recreate a route.

Apple Watch workout routes from Apple Health

Apple Watch users do not need a GPX file. With your permission, LensPin reads existing workout routes directly from Apple Health through read-only HealthKit access and matches photo times to route positions. No export or sync through another service is needed. A workout without a recorded route cannot provide positions.

Camera clock offsets affect the matching preview

A fast or slow camera clock, or a time-zone difference, can shift a match along the trip. LensPin previews a fixed camera clock offset without changing capture dates. Time-zone display options control how times appear. Check different cameras and periods with changed clocks separately.

Understand the match categories

  • High confidence

    Clues are close in time and consistent. Selected by default, pending your confirmation.

  • Review

    Clues may be sparse, one-sided or conflicting. Inspect the explanation before selecting.

  • No clear suggestion

    The available clues are insufficient. Check the nearest references and leave the photo unchanged if you cannot confirm a place.

How the location clues agree

When a track and nearby geotagged photos are both available, LensPin compares the photo’s saved location with the track’s estimated location at that photo’s capture time. It uses a nearby reference in the same track segment and within the matching time window. A verified iPhone photo within 100 m strengthens the suggestion. A difference over 100 m and up to 300 m leaves the track’s confidence unchanged; another camera’s photo within 100 m also leaves it unchanged. Over 300 m means the clues conflict and the suggestion needs review. Time gaps, track coverage and your confidence settings also affect the result.

Review each suggestion, then save to the library

Check each suggestion’s map, reference photos and time gaps before approving it. Processing stays on device. Saving updates the location in the Photos library, leaves original files unchanged, and never overwrites existing locations.
